title: In TESS data, large flares on CPV hosts come with dip-pattern changes that transplanted flares do not reproduce; hosts flare 1.6 times more than matched rotators; flares do not prefer dip phases
abstract: We test whether stellar flares are connected to the corotating material of complex periodic variables (CPVs). We used 3,283 TESS 2-minute light curves (sectors 1-107) of 149 CPV hosts and 1,597 matched rapid rotators (P = 0.15-1 d, BP-RP = 2.4-3.8), with 19,324 flares from a phase-template method and injection-recovery. A superposed-epoch test measures the change of the folded shape across each flare as a percentile u among flare-free rotations (null 0.5). For 264 flares with equivalent duration of 100 s or more in sectors with the CPV pattern, u = 0.593 (0.554-0.630) for the dip component and 0.606 for the spot component. The same flares transplanted to random times, with the full pipeline rerun, give 0.481 and 0.466. The excess is three times larger than in comparison stars and survives gap, window, impulsive-flare and out-of-dip variants. But flares account for only 3-5% of large dip changes, and the sign of the dip-power change is not robust. Hosts flare 1.66 (1.44-1.85) times more often at fixed age class, colour, period and noise (1.41 with more covariates); template-mismatch events are not more frequent. Inside hosts, CPV sectors do not have more flares, and flares occur uniformly in phase relative to the dips. Thus the material changes with the magnetic events that large flares mark, but flares do not drive most dip evolution. Limitations: the test is symmetric in time, labels come from one emulated vetter, and comparison stars have smaller features. Code, derived tables and hashes are included; TESS FITS files are not.
